compareCandidate.label: Population vs. community
compareCandidate.description: A population is one species in an area. A community is all the different populations (all species) living together there.

plainLanguageExplanation: A population is a group of organisms of the same species that live in the same place at the same time. All the dandelions in one field, all the squirrels in one forest - each is a population. Populations grow when births and new arrivals outnumber deaths and departures, and they shrink when the reverse happens. Population size can be limited by food, water, space, disease, and predators. Studying populations helps us understand how species are doing and what an area can support.

keyFacts.label: Definition
keyFacts.value: A group of the same species in the same place at the same time

keyFacts.label: Grows when
keyFacts.value: Births and arrivals outnumber deaths and departures

keyFacts.label: Shrinks when
keyFacts.value: Deaths and departures outnumber births and arrivals

keyFacts.label: Limits
keyFacts.value: Food, water, space, disease, and predators limit size

keyFacts.label: Example
keyFacts.value: All the robins in a park are a robin population

whyItMatters: Populations are how we count life and track whether a species is doing well. Understanding populations explains why some animals boom and crash, why invasive species spread, and how scientists measure the health of the natural world.
didYouKnow: The human population recently passed 8 billion people - that's one population of one species covering the whole planet.
